9.0.0.en: In his grief over his people Jeremiah began to weep for them, and even wished to keep weeping without ceasing, wishing that his head were turned into water and his eyes into a fountain, so that he might weep continually for those of his people who perish because of their evil. He calls Jerusalem “the daughter of my people,” since her natural position is to be the bride of God, but she turned aside into evil, therefore her sons will perish.

9.1.0.en: A lodging place of wayfaring men: an inn.

9.1.1.en: Since the prophet could not bear the sight of his people sunk in sin and about to perish, he wished to go far away into the wilderness and find a place to dwell, so as not to see the adultery spread among his people, whether bodily adultery, or spiritual adultery by the worship of idols and betrayal of God.

9.1.2.en: Your tears for your sins, or for the sins of others, are very precious to God, because they mean your love for God and for others, and your repentance and your rejection of evil. So let your feelings flow during prayer, and confess your sins every day before God, and pray for those who sin around you.

9.2.0.en: Their bow: the bow used in war to shoot arrows.

9.2.1.en: He compares the tongues of his people to bows that shoot arrows in war, as an expression of the sharpness of their speech and their evil and their falling into lying, with which they wound the feelings of those around them and trouble them. They felt that lying gives them strength and material gain, so they persisted in it and refused to repent.

9.3.0.en: Will utterly supplant: the heel is the back of a person's foot, and to supplant means to pursue him and follow his heels in order to make him fall and achieve one's personal gains.

9.3.1.en: Slander: spreading false words about a certain person among others.

9.3.2.en: He alerts the people to the lack of sincerity that has spread among them and the abundance of lying, so that a person cannot trust his brother, for all have become deceivers. Also each one follows the heels of the other in selfishness and looks for his own interest even at the expense of others, and stirs up rumors and false accusations against the innocent to achieve his gains.

9.4.0.en: Deceive: he deceives him, exploiting his unawareness.

9.4.1.en: It shows their persistence in lying and deceit: one exploits the other's trust in him, deceives him and attacks him, and plans plots in which he toils to accomplish his evils. And instead of toiling to acquire virtues, he toils many times over to acquire evil.

9.4.2.en: Give up your rights, and drive away evil thoughts, and do not be led by the provocations that meet you, so that you keep your peace and direct your energy to positive work, that is, drawing near to God and loving others, and so achieve benefit for yourself and for those around you.

9.5.0.en: He rebukes his people, showing their plunging into lying, and says to them that they dwelt “in the midst of deceit,” and since they plunged into evil they thereby refused to know God, for to know sin is to drive God out of the heart, and the opposite is true: to know God drives out sin.

9.6.0.en: Since God sees their insistence on lying and deceit, He finds no means of rescuing them except to allow their discipline through the Babylonian attack, that perhaps they will repent. And He addresses Jerusalem in fatherhood, calling her the daughter of His people, perhaps to stir her love toward Him. For affliction tests a person and shows him the result of his sin, so he repents and is purified from it.

9.7.0.en: He compares their lying tongue to an arrow that kills others, because it speaks words of love to the friend and at the same time plots against him to kill him or exploit him, as Judas Iscariot did when he betrayed Christ to death with a kiss.

9.8.0.en: God makes them witnesses against themselves, and indeed He calls the whole world to witness that His people who insist on lying deserve punishment and vengeance for their evil. He does not take vengeance on His children whom He loves, but He hates their evils and takes vengeance on them by afflictions, showing their hideousness so that His children hate them.

9.9.0.en: The prophet Jeremiah shows his grief over Jerusalem and the land of Judea around her because of the ruin coming upon them at the hands of the Babylonians, who burned them, so they turned into a deserted land through which no man passes and no cattle graze, and even the birds keep away from it because it has become a ruin. He proclaims this prophecy, not only that his heart may ache, but that perhaps he may move the hearts of his people, so that they fear the destruction coming upon them and return to God.

9.10.0.en: Dragons: an animal larger than the fox and smaller than the wolf that always howls, characterized by deceit and cunning, and lives in deserted places.

9.10.1.en: He continues the description of Jerusalem and Judea and says that they will become heaps of stones and dust, and wild animals such as jackals will spread in them, and no man will dwell in them.

9.11.0.en: God asks, searching for a spiritual man whom He loves, to whom He reveals His wisdom concerning the affliction that He will allow on the kingdom of Judah, so that he understands and declares the wisdom of God to others, that perhaps they will repent. And this wise and spiritual man is the prophet Jeremiah, and a small number of those who lived with God in the midst of the evils of the kingdom of Judah.

9.12.0.en: God declares the reason for the affliction, which is the rejection by His people of His commandments and His law, and their being led after idols and evil lusts.

9.12.1.en: You can become wise and understand God's purposes in the events that pass over you if you walk in humility before Him, and always seek His guidance, and live a life of repentance and purity. And when you receive this wisdom you stand firm in faith and call others to enjoy fellowship with God and to be saved from evil.

9.13.0.en: Baalim: the plural of Baal, a pagan god of the Canaanites called the god of fertility and farms, who spread in their various lands and each city called him by its own name, such as Baal-peor. And since the Jews lived among the Canaanites they also worshiped the Baalim.

9.13.1.en: God continues the reason for the ruin coming upon them, which is their stubbornness, that is, their insistence on evil and their holding fast to the worship of idols, the most famous of which is the worship of the Baalim that they received from their fathers; that is, the people of God rejected Him through the years and worshiped idols, so they deserved this discipline.

9.14.0.en: Wormwood: a plant that grows in Palestine, whose juice is bitter and poisonous.

9.14.1.en: God declares His power and calls Himself the LORD of hosts, and declares His special attachment to His people, saying the God of Israel, that is, that He is the powerful and loving God who will discipline His people; and He borrows the names of hated plants that grow in Palestine whose juice is bitter and poisonous, as an indication of the severity of His discipline.

9.15.0.en: When the Babylonians attack, they will not only destroy the kingdom of Judah, but will transfer the people and scatter them in the world to abolish their nationality and belonging, after they kill many of them by weakening and frightening them.

9.16.0.en: Mourning women: women who specialize in stirring the feelings of the grieving at the passing of their loved ones, who cry out with words that move hearts and make everyone weep.

9.16.1.en: Cunning women: women distinguished in understanding, intellect and discernment of matters.

9.16.2.en: The prophet calls for weeping over Jerusalem and for the proclaiming of words of grief, that is, a lament over her, using those who specialize in that, who are the mourning women and the cunning women, so as to move the feelings of all to weep over her, that perhaps this will bring them back to God in repentance.

9.17.0.en: Zion: its meaning is fortress, and its name is applied to the mountain on which Jerusalem was built, so what is meant by Zion is Jerusalem.

9.17.1.en: God shows the grief of His people when the army of Babylon attacked them, so they fled before them in shame, and began to lament their condition in sorrow.

9.18.0.en: He calls the women of the Jews to lament Jerusalem and teach their daughters how to grieve over her, because the army of Babylon has attacked their houses, so they leaped from the windows, and killed those in the houses, and likewise the children who play around the houses and the young men who work and move about in the squares, that is, death has attacked everyone.

9.19.0.en: He expresses the multitude of the slain by saying that their corpses will be cast on the fields like the dung of man or beast, or like a handful of the harvest that the farmer gathers, which falls from him behind him, and being occupied with gathering the harvest he does not care about the little that falls. So there will be many slain and no one will gather their corpses when Babylon attacks.

9.19.1.en: May you weep over your sins that caused you many pains, so that you do not repeat them, and guard against them afterwards, and ask God's forgiveness, and so you obtain many divine mercies.

9.20.0.en: God warns His people not to rely on their wisdom, or their strength, or their riches, for all are passing human things, but to rely on God with humility, and He will protect them; for what did their wisdom and strength and riches profit them before the Babylonian attack?..! Of course they profited nothing because of their sins and their distance from God.

9.21.0.en: He makes clear that glory and boasting are in knowing God and living with Him, so God protects him and fills him with peace and delivers him from all evil and rejoices in him.

9.21.1.en: Thank God for all His gifts, for they are from Him and not from you, and seek Him before every work, and He will be with you, and your reliance on Him and your enjoyment of fellowship with Him will increase.

9.22.0.en: God declares that He will soon punish the kingdom of Judah for their evil, and though they are circumcised in the flesh, their hearts are still full of evil; and after that He will punish the pagan Gentiles, uncircumcised in the flesh, for their evil, for the reason for punishment and discipline is always sin. And God is long-suffering toward the wicked, that perhaps they will take warning from the discipline of other wicked people and return to Him.

9.23.0.en: Egypt: it was the first empire in the world, and after the rise of the Assyrian kingdom in its place it was still strong, and the Jews thought that resorting to it would deliver them from any evil. Judah: the kingdom of Judah, that is, the southern kingdom of the Jews.

9.23.1.en: Edom: the descendants of Esau who live in the mountains of Seir.

9.23.2.en: The children of Ammon: the descendants of Lot, who are neighbors of the Jews.

9.23.3.en: Moab: the descendants of Lot, who are also neighbors of the Jews.

9.23.4.en: That are in the utmost corners: in ancient times men used to cut their hair on all sides of their heads and leave a circle of hair on top of their heads to please some pagan gods, which means that they are followers of this pagan god.

9.23.5.en: God declares His wrath against the pagan nations such as Egypt, Edom, the children of Ammon and Moab because of the inclinations of their evil hearts, and likewise against the Jews because of their evil although they are circumcised in the flesh.

9.23.6.en: The appearance of your life in the Church and your having good outward qualities is not enough for the salvation of your soul. So do not care about people's opinion, but purify your heart by repentance to live with God and enjoy His salvation. Returning to God

10.0.0.en: The way of the heathen: the worship of idols.

10.0.1.en: The signs of heaven: the movements of the planets and the sun in a great and marvelous manner, so that you worship them. God warns His people against being led into the worship of idols like the surrounding nations, and against fearing their authority, and among these worships is the worship of the planets and the sky.

10.1.0.en: The customs of the people: the pagan worships of the nations.

10.1.1.en: The forest: the desert and the desolate place.

10.1.3.en: God alerts them that what the nations worship of idols is nothing but pieces of wood from a tree cut down from the desert, or any place, which the carpenter then turned into a statue using the axe and the tools of carpentry.

10.2.0.en: He shows the weakness of these statues in that they are adorned with precious metals of silver and gold, and they give them splendor and glory, and so that they do not break easily they fasten them with nails, and strike on them with hammers, that is, mallets, until they become a statue of any person.

10.3.0.en: The palm tree: the scarecrow, which is two crossed pieces of wood on which a robe is hung that the wind moves, so the birds think it is a person and fly away and keep off the field and do not harm the crop.

10.3.1.en: A cucumber field: a field planted with cucumbers (gourds). God makes clear the weakness of these statues, and compares them to the scarecrow that farmers place in their fields to drive away the harmful birds that eat their fruits, for this statue is like the scarecrow, merely a sight with no life in it, and these pagan gods are helpless and cannot walk, so those who worship them carry them, and consequently they are worthless, they harm no one and do no good to anyone.

10.4.0.en: On the other hand the prophet Jeremiah declares that God is above all these pagan gods and there is no room for comparison with Him in might and power.

10.5.0.en: To thee doth it appertain: glory and fear and reverence are fitting for You.

10.5.1.en: Jeremiah declares that God is the King of all the peoples of the world, and not the pagan gods, and He deserves fear and respect.

10.6.1.en: The doctrine of vanities: the vain pagan worships with all their customs and rites.

10.6.2.en: Everyone who worships idols is ignorant and his worship is vain, because he worships a piece of wood made by human hands and leaves God, the true God.

10.7.0.en: Hammer: hammers are used for beating and shaping metals such as silver and gold.

10.7.1.en: Tarshish: a city in Spain at the end of the Mediterranean Sea, famous for trade, and considered the end of the known world at that time.

10.7.2.en: Uphaz: also called Ophir, a place in the south of the Arabian Peninsula near Yemen, famous for the production of gold.

10.7.3.en: Blue: cloth of a blue color.

10.7.6.en: He declares that the greatness of these statues is due to their being covered with silver and gold and dressed in the garments of the great, of blue and red colors.

10.8.0.en: Jeremiah declares the great attributes of God, which are:

10.8.4.en: 4- A mighty God, whose wrath destroys all the wicked.

10.9.0.en: If God is great to this degree, then the pagan gods, who did not create the heavens and the earth and did not do anything, since they are mere statues, will pass away, but God will remain.

10.10.0.en: God is the Creator of the whole world, both the earth and the heavens and all who dwell and live in them.

10.11.0.en: He declares that God is the Controller of all, who moves the clouds, which are a quantity of evaporated water, and moves them from the end of the earth to its ends, and directs the winds from place to place, for they go out by the command of God, so He makes this clear by saying that they come out of His treasures, that is, by His command and from Him.

10.12.0.en: The ignorance of every man appeared because of his reliance on his personal knowledge, and indeed everyone who relied on the pagan gods felt embarrassment and shame, because they will not profit him in the time of affliction.

10.13.0.en: The vanity and weakness of the pagan gods appears in that when God punishes the pagans their gods do not profit them, but are shattered and perish with them.

10.14.0.en: He declares that God is the God of Jacob, that is, Israel, and He is not like these weak pagan gods but is the Creator and Former of all that exists, and He is King over His people Israel, to whom He gives for their faith in Him the eternal inheritance, and He expresses His kingship by the scepter of the king, and then in the end He declares His power by describing Himself as the LORD of hosts; and by this He calls the people of God to keep away from the worship of vain idols and to hold fast to the worship of the powerful God who lives forever, who gives them the Kingdom of Heaven.

10.14.1.en: Everything to which people attach themselves, whether money, or position, or relationships ... all of them are passing things, so do not be occupied with them, but let your heart cling to God, who fills you with peace and in the end gives you eternal life with Him.

10.15.0.en: Thy wares: the belongings of each individual that he carries on his shoulder in a bundle to go into captivity.

10.15.1.en: God calls to Jerusalem, besieged by the army of Babylon, that each one of her inhabitants gather his own belongings, because they will be taken captive and driven out from Jerusalem to the lands of the kingdom of Babylon.

10.16.0.en: God declares that He will strike the inhabitants of the land of the kingdom of Judah by the armies of Babylon, which will strike them with stones by slings, and with all weapons such as arrows and spears, that perhaps when they feel this calamity they will return to God and repent of their sins that caused them this affliction.

10.17.0.en: Jerusalem cries out because she has been ruined by Babylon, so she is crushed and destroyed and struck with blows that have no cure, and she has nothing before her but to bear this ruin, and understand God's purpose and repent.

10.18.0.en: My cords: the ropes tied to the cloth of the tent and ending in the stake fixed in the ground; the longer these ropes are, the wider the shade under the tent.

10.18.1.en: My curtains: pieces of cloth that together make the tent.

10.18.2.en: He compares Jerusalem to a tent, so that when the army of Babylon attacks her this tent is ruined and torn down and its ropes cut, and her sons flee from her and there is no one to defend her.

10.19.0.en: Dragons: an animal smaller than the wolf and larger than the fox, which devours whoever meets it.

10.19.1.en: He makes clear the attack of Babylon coming from the north by the cry of the army that destroyed Jerusalem and Judea and made them a ruin without inhabitant, so wild beasts such as jackals dwelt in them.

10.19.2.en: Pay attention to God's warnings so that you repent of your sins, and keep away from evil, and prepare for eternal life, and guard against the attacks of the devil by the holy life in the Church, so that you live in security and grow in the way of God.

10.20.0.en: Jeremiah declares on behalf of the people of God his weakness as a man who cannot know the way of eternal life except with the help of God.

10.21.0.en: He also declares his repentance and his need for punishment as a discipline from God so that he returns to Him, which is the discipline of a father for his son without destroying him, that is, discipline with His mercy. What is meant by judgment is the fatherly love and mercy, while anger means the punishment for the destruction of the wicked.

10.22.0.en: If God has allowed the Gentiles in the form of Babylon to discipline the people of God that they may repent, He will afterwards punish them with severe wrath to destroy them, because they insist on rejecting God and faith in Him. For God's discipline of His children is so that they repent, while His wrath on the wicked nations is for their destruction.

10.22.1.en: I thank You, O Lord, because You are tender to me even in Your punishment, to call me to repentance. So remove by discipline every inclination within me toward evil, that I may know You and love You, and advance in Your way to the Kingdom.
